newsitem.title: USA: Insignia restates results, to restructure.
newsitem.headline: Insignia restates results, to restructure.

text.p: Insignia Solutions Plc said Thursday that it is restating its first and second quarter results after finding irregularities in the reporting of sales contracts and reseller inventories.

The company said additionally that it has restructured its operations to integrate development, marketing and sales of its two major product lines and has formed two business units: an NTRIGUE Business Group and a SoftWindows Business Group.

The NTRIGUE group will focus on leading-edge products for intranet and Internet Windows NT remote access solutions, and the SoftWindows group will focus on worldwide sales and marketing of the SoftWindows product line, the company said.

The company said a restatement of results comes after finding that some individuals had entered into unauthorized pacts with certain distributors and resellers and failed to accurately report on unsold inventories.

For the first quarter, ended March 31, 1996, restated revenues are $13.1 million, compared with previously reported revenues of $14.7 million. The net loss is $225,000, or $0.02 per share, compared with a previously reported net profit of $749,000, or $0.06 per share.

For the second quarter, ended June 30, 1996, restated revenues are $14.9 million, compared with previously reported revenues of $15.7 million. Restated net income is $569,000, or $0.04 per share, versus previously reported net of $1.5 million, or $0.11 per share, the company said.

The company reported a net loss of $6.1 million, or $0.53 per share for the fourth quarter 1996, on revenues of $7.2 million. The year-ago figures were a profit of $630,000, or $0.05 per share on revenues of $14 million.

For the full year 1996, revenues were $44.2 million, compared with $55.1 million in 1995, and the net loss was $10.8 million, or $0.95 per share, versus net profit of $5.3 million, or $0.45 per share, in 1995.
The company said that at the direction of the Audit Committee on its Board, it is implementing additional accounting and reporting controls to help prevent future breaches of company policies.
It said that restructuring should help it refocus and improve its operations.
"We believe this reorganization will give the company the focus it needs to market, sell and continue to improve our existing product lines," the company said in a release.
